name: Nullsec Vulnerability Taxonomy
description: Canonical vulnerability categories for Nullsec-1. Each category maps to a deterministic check dimension used by the post-inference validator.

categories.title: Exposed Secret / Credential
categories.description: Hardcoded API keys, private keys, tokens, passwords, or secrets committed to source, logs, or client-shipped code.

categories.title: Broken or Missing Authentication
categories.description: Endpoints, routes, or functions that perform sensitive actions without verifying identity, or with bypassable/weak auth.

categories.title: Missing Rate Limiting
categories.description: Public or expensive endpoints (auth, LLM calls, payments, email) with no throttling, enabling abuse, brute force, or cost amplification.

categories.title: Unsafe Admin Route
categories.description: Administrative or privileged routes lacking role checks, exposed in client bundles, or reachable without elevation.

categories.title: SQL Injection
categories.description: User-controlled input concatenated into SQL queries instead of parameterized.

categories.title: Cross-Site Scripting
categories.description: Unsanitized user input rendered into HTML/DOM, enabling script execution.

categories.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
categories.description: Server makes outbound requests to user-controlled URLs without allowlist, reaching internal services or metadata endpoints.

categories.title: OS Command Injection
categories.description: User input passed to shell/OS command execution without sanitization.

categories.title: Unsafe File Upload / Path Traversal
categories.description: Uploads without type/size validation, or file paths built from user input enabling traversal or RCE.

categories.title: Prompt Injection
categories.description: Untrusted content (user input, web pages, tool results, files) concatenated into LLM prompts/system instructions without isolation, enabling instruction hijacking.

categories.title: MCP Tool Abuse
categories.description: MCP tools exposed with overbroad scope, no auth on the server, dangerous capabilities (fs/shell/network) without confirmation, or tool descriptions that can be poisoned.

categories.title: Dangerous Shell Command
categories.description: Destructive or unguarded shell invocations (rm -rf, curl | sh, chmod 777) in scripts, CI, or agent tool calls.

categories.title: Wallet / Transaction Risk
categories.description: Private keys in code/env shipped to client, unsigned/unbounded transactions, missing simulation, no slippage/amount checks, or seed phrases in logs.

categories.title: Smart Contract Risk
categories.description: Reentrancy, missing access modifiers, unchecked external calls, integer issues, or unsafe delegatecall in on-chain code.

categories.title: Dependency / Supply-Chain Risk
categories.description: Known-vulnerable, unpinned, typosquatted, or postinstall-script dependencies; install from untrusted sources.

categories.title: Environment / Configuration Exposure
categories.description: Environment files, server configuration, debug settings, source maps, or cloud metadata exposed to untrusted parties — e.g. a .env served from a public directory, server secrets bundled into a frontend build, debug config enabled in production, source maps leaking internal env names, or cloud instance-metadata leakage.

dimension_notes.summary: check_dimensions are the 8 axes every verdict must report on. They are NOT categories. A category is a specific vulnerability class and maps to exactly one primary check_dimension.
dimension_notes.input_validation: DIMENSION, not a category. Categories that exercise it include SQL_INJECTION, XSS, SSRF, UNSAFE_FILE_UPLOAD, PROMPT_INJECTION, SMART_CONTRACT_RISK.
dimension_notes.environment_exposure: DIMENSION and (as of v1.1.0) also the primary dimension of the ENVIRONMENT_EXPOSURE category.
